description_full: ExlService Holdings, Inc., operates as a data and artificial intelligence (AI) company in the North America, the United Kingdom, Europe, and internationally. The company operates through Insurance; Healthcare and Life Sciences; Banking, Capital Markets, and Diversified Industries; and International Growth Markets. It provides digital operations and solutions and analytics-driven services, such as claims management, premium and benefit administration, agency management, account reconciliation, actuarial and risk analytics, policy research, digital marketing, underwriting support, new business acquisition, policy servicing, audit, surveys, billing and collection, commercial and residential survey, and customer service; digital customer acquisition services using a software-as-a-service delivery model through LifePRO and Life Digital Suite platforms; and Subrosource software platform, an end-to-end subrogation platform. The company also offers health care services for care, utilization, and disease management; payment integrity; revenue optimization, customer engagement, and commercial analytics and regulatory support services; and digital operations and solutions. In addition, it provides financial planning and analysis, accounting, regulatory and statutory reporting, decision support, data management, and compliance services; consumer and commercial banking, credit card and payment services; fintech, wealth and retirement services; capital markets, utilities, retail and consumer packaged goods, communications, media and entertainment, travel and leisure, transportation and logistics, infrastructure, and other business services; property and casualty insurance, life insurance, disability insurance; and insurance brokers, reinsurers, annuity and retirement services. The company was founded in 1999 and is headquartered in New York, New York.
ceo_bio: Mr. Rohit  Kapoor | Co-Founder, Chairman & CEO | Age 60 | Compensation: $2.4M (FY2025)
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 65K people. Revenue per employee of $32K ranks in the bottom quartile among Technology peers, with revenue growing 13%/yr across its filed history. Each employee generates $5K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $1K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 74× revenue per employee (elevated relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags low compensation governance risk (1/10).
financial_summary: ExlService Holdings, Inc. is a mid-cap technology business with a $6.5B market cap on $2.1B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +14% over the past three years and +13% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 24% against a 9% cost of capital — a 15-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 37%.

The business throws off $298M in free cash flow — roughly 14 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.40× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 18× is fortress-like.
Shareholder yield of 4.9% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 2.7% of the shares.

sect: Its 15% operating margin runs 8pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It earns less of the sector's profit than its revenue share would suggest (0.64x).
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+5.6% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 533 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted lower, down 7% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has rebounded 22% over the last three months.
The price sits near the top of its 52-week range, 3% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 42% and a beta of 0.95, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 0.28 vs 5y 0.93), so read it loosely.
About $73.7M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 46% in the 2020 crash, 22% in the 2022 bear market and 78% in 2008.
val: The stock trades only 8% below its DCF fair value of $47.21, a thin margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 45%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $29.83 to $77.52 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 18% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 4.6% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 4.6% (vs the 8% bar).
The 8 covering analysts target $48.62 on average, 12% above the price.
The price implies 11.5% annual cash-flow growth, 2pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 24% clears the cost of capital of 9.2% by 15pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.33).
It runs a 37% gross margin and converts 14% of revenue into free cash flow, or 10% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 8/9 and cash conversion of 1.40x.
ROE of 28% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.9x equity multiplier).
It spends 3.8% of revenue on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $29.8M (0% of market cap).
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 8.4, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 13.9% over 3 years, 16.8% over 5 years and 12.8% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded 13.1% a year over five years.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (0.9x, 2.5% of sales), a maintenance pace.
Its Rule of 40 score is 27, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own a modest 2.7%, and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insiders have only sold over the past year (8 sales, net $2.8M sold).
It returns 4.9% a year to shareholders (4.9% in buybacks).
The share count has shrunk 1.9% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 65,000 employees, each generates about $32K of revenue, 0.1x the Technology median, and revenue has grown 13.4% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $5K of free cash flow per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
CEO pay is $2.4M (74x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (1/10, lower is better).
